newsitem.title: GERMANY: German committee starts talks on tax reforms.
newsitem.headline: German committee starts talks on tax reforms.

text.p: Germany's parliamentary mediation committee met on Wednesday to discuss government tax reforms but hopes of a deal with the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) have already faded after preliminary talks.

The mediation committee, called by the government's lower house majority after the SPD voted down Finance Minister Theo Waigel's tax reform in the Bundesrat upper chamber, began its meeting after a 90-minute delay.
Negotiators from both sides declared Waigel's plan to slash income and corporate taxes effectively dead for the duration of the current parliament after two days of informal talks made no progress.
Arriving for the meeting, Waigel said the SPD wanted "absolutely intentionally" to make the tax reform fail.

Negotiators said they saw some chance of ending a two-year row over abolishing a capital trading tax on companies, but the government side rejects SPD financing proposals for a cut in occupational insurance charges intended to boost job creation.
Chances of a deal here looked to suffer a last-minute blow when some SPD negotiators emerged from a meeting on Wednesday morning saying they wanted to link the two issues.
The SPD majority in the mediation committee is certain to vote down the tax reform, sending it back to the Bundestag lower house, which will hold a special session next Tuesday.
